title: Group: legal entity register and organization charts
what_it_shows: Cris Santos Company Holdings, Inc. is a publicly traded SEC registrant (large accelerated filer). Cloud Hosting, Managed IT and Consulting, and Payment Processing are separate legal subsidiaries under common ownership; corporate shared services (identity, security operations, the group landing zone, HR, finance, legal, risk, privacy and internal audit) sit in the parent. Licenses held are the Payment Processing state money transmitter licenses for bill pay; the register lists no bank charter, no New York financial services license, no broker-dealer or investment adviser registration, no insurance license and no 42 CFR Part 2 program. Organization charts show the Group CISO, Group Chief Risk Officer, Group Chief Privacy Officer and Group General Counsel; division CISOs in Cloud Hosting and Payment Processing; a security and compliance lead and a federal contracts compliance officer in Managed IT; the Government Cloud compliance director; group internal audit reporting to the board audit committee; the disclosure committee; and the Group AI council

title: Group: HR roster by division
what_it_shows: 45,000 employees with work locations in 46 states and none in a country of concern under 28 CFR Part 202: Cloud Hosting about 21,000, Managed IT and Consulting about 12,000 (about 6,800 managed services engineers), Payment Processing about 7,000 (division security team of about 140), corporate shared services about 5,000 (about 260 SOC analysts in three sites). About 1,400 contractors in addition. G1 operations staff are recorded as U.S. persons. Termination events feed SYS-G1 identity governance

title: Group: FY2025 revenue by division and payment volumes
what_it_shows: FY2025 revenue about $18.0 billion: Cloud Hosting about $10.2 billion, Managed IT and Consulting about $4.8 billion, Payment Processing about $3.0 billion in net revenue. Payment Processing moved about $1.9 billion of merchant and biller funds per business day

title: Group: Form 10-K cybersecurity disclosure (Reg S-K Item 106)
what_it_shows: The FY2025 annual report describes board risk committee oversight of cyber risk, the Group CISO's reporting line, and the use of independent assessors (group internal audit, the FedRAMP assessment service and the PCI QSA).

title: Group: board committee charters, 2025 to 2026 minutes and risk acceptance standard
what_it_shows: The board risk committee oversees group cyber and AI risk each quarter and alone accepts Very High risks; the board audit committee oversees internal audit and SEC reporting. The disclosure committee charter covers Form 8-K Item 1.05 materiality determinations for cybersecurity incidents. The risk acceptance standard sets Very Low and Low to the division security lead, Moderate to the division president, and High to the Group Chief Risk Officer with the Group CISO, reported to the board risk committee

title: Group: identity platform authentication and session policy export (SYS-G1)
what_it_shows: Every workforce identity signs in through single sign-on with MFA; number matching is required where hardware keys are not used. Group, Cloud Hosting and Payment Processing administrators and HCP privileged roles use phishing-resistant hardware keys. Workforce HCP console sessions end after 8 hours, with re-authentication for privileged actions. Lockout and risk-based sign-in blocking are enabled. The Managed IT legacy identity tenant federates into SYS-G1 and into the HCP partner-operator path; it accepts push MFA and issues 12-hour sessions that are not bound to a device. G1 accepts agency federation with PIV-based credentials

title: Group: identity governance configuration, joiner-mover-leaver workflows and break-glass log
what_it_shows: Joiner-mover-leaver workflows run from HR events for all divisions; accounts are disabled within 4 hours of the termination event (immediately for involuntary terminations) and after 45 days of inactivity; temporary and emergency accounts expire after 30 days by default; identifiers are unique and never reused; administrators hold separate privileged identities. Sealed break-glass accounts exist per critical system (HCP, fleet, CDE, RMM) and the log shows quarterly tests, with passwords rotated after every use. Managed IT technician and partner-operator identities live in the legacy tenant, outside these workflows; its leaver processing runs the next business day. Workforce identities are proofed at hire

title: Group: Q1 2026 access certification report
what_it_shows: The Q1 2026 campaign certified group application roles and HCP roles and privileged groups (managers and the HCP system owner). Partner-operator grants, legacy-tenant accounts and RMM technician accounts were not in the campaign

title: Group: privileged access management configuration and role matrix
what_it_shows: Privileged access for group, Cloud Hosting and Payment Processing administrators is granted just in time through PAM, with approval and session recording, and expires after 4 hours. About 2,300 of the about 6,400 Cloud Hosting workforce members with HCP roles can request privileged access. PAM roles separate approvers from users; production deployments need an author and an approver. CDE roles are available only through PAM. Partner-operator access is not brokered by PAM. Bastion sessions to hypervisor managers and BMCs, including escorted vendor sessions, are recorded

title: Group: device management policy and endpoint compliance report
what_it_shows: Managed laptops are encrypted, enrolled in EDR, can be wiped remotely, and lock after 10 minutes idle. Remote administrative access to HCP management networks goes through the SYS-G1 access broker from managed devices with MFA; there is no VPN path into those networks

title: Group: EDR coverage report
what_it_shows: EDR reports on all workforce endpoints, HCP hosts and administrator workstations, and division workloads, including the CDE, the CDE connected-to systems and the SYS-M2 enclave. Managed client servers carry EDR where the client contract includes it

title: Group: SIEM data sources, detection catalog and correlation rules
what_it_shows: The 24x7 SOC ingests HCP audit logs, SYS-G1, EDR, network flows, landing-zone and CDE logs; G1 sends only security logs over a dedicated path. Correlation rules and SOAR playbooks span divisions; user behavior analytics cover SYS-G1 identities and HCP administrator actions. Run-command executions are logged with identity, tenant and command hash, and the catalog has no rule on run-command volume or spread across tenants. RMM audit logs are not a SIEM source. Advisories from CISA and vendors are logged and assigned

title: Group: AI triage configuration, SOAR action list and auto-close statistics
what_it_shows: The AI triage service has been enabled since 2025-11. In Q1 2026 it auto-closed about 64% of alerts across all divisions, including CDE and G1 sources. Seven SOAR containment actions can run without a human: isolate a host, disable a workforce account, revoke sessions, block an address, quarantine a file, suspend a cloud workload, and reset credentials. Alert context, which can include G1 resource metadata and customer IP addresses, is sent to a third-party hosted model service under no-training and no-retention terms. Analysts review High-severity alerts. No accuracy validation records by division were provided, and no division approval of unattended action classes is on file

title: Group: SOC playbooks, exercise reports and case system export, 2025 to 2026
what_it_shows: HCP-specific and technical playbooks exist and were exercised each quarter; no exercise recorded crosses divisions or uses a group notification matrix. Cases carry discovery and determination timestamps per notifying entity. Managed IT handles single-client RMM incidents in its own ticketing, outside the SOC case system. Incident responders and division liaisons train each year, with role modules for G1 federal incident response coordinators

title: Group: incident response plan (2026 edition)
what_it_shows: The group plan sets the incident severity scale, the incident commander role and the plan's distribution and protection. It does not define FedRAMP Reportable Incidents, DFARS cyber incidents or bank notification incidents in one place, and it does not describe the automated containment actions the AI triage service has taken since 2025-11

title: Group: notification procedures by division
what_it_shows: Notice procedures are kept by division: Cloud Hosting customer, bank and BAA notices; Managed IT client, BAA, bank and DIBNet steps; the Payment Processing incident response plan with card network and sponsor bank steps; and the disclosure committee step for Form 8-K Item 1.05. No single group matrix lists FedRAMP incident reports, DFARS 72-hour reports, bank service provider notices, HIPAA business associate notices, sponsor bank and card network notices, the FTC Safeguards notice and SEC materiality together, and no exercise of these procedures across divisions is recorded

title: Group: vulnerability management standard, scan configuration and KEV report
what_it_shows: The vulnerability standard sets CVSS-based remediation targets (critical 15 days, high 30 days, moderate 90 days). Authenticated scans run weekly on hosts and continuously on container images; network devices and BMCs are scanned monthly. KEV entries are matched daily and open tickets automatically

title: Group: policy library (2025 group policies, group standards and division supplements)
what_it_shows: The 2025 group policies are aligned to NIST CSF 2.0 and published on the intranet with annual acknowledgment; the policy review log shows policies, procedures and people-based processes reviewed once a year. Group standards cover logging (events, review, and retention of 1 year searchable and 7 years archived), change and configuration, contingency, personnel security, risk assessment (NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1), training, and the retention schedule. Supplements exist for Cloud Hosting, Managed IT (v2024, EV-065) and Payment Processing. The library has no AI standard until the Group AI Standard (EV-030)

title: Group: common control catalog and inheritance records
what_it_shows: The catalog lists 83 controls provided by group functions (SYS-G1, SYS-G2, SYS-G3, group HR) or by Cloud Hosting data center operations and the edge service, with named control owners. Inheritance is documented for Cloud Hosting (G1 FedRAMP package and SL-1 SOC 2 system description) and for Payment Processing (PCI DSS responsibility matrix for group services, which does not list the SL-1 platform controls). No inheritance record was provided for Managed IT

title: Group: landing zone account inventory, IAM export, guardrails and hub firewall policy
what_it_shows: The group landing zone runs on SL-1: dedicated Payment Processing CDE accounts in R1 and R3, Managed IT ticketing and client access broker accounts, and corporate accounts. Roles are federated from SYS-G1 and accounts have no local users except sealed break-glass accounts. Guardrails block public storage, unencrypted volumes and unapproved regions; the hub firewall denies traffic between division accounts by default

title: Group: key management design and key policy export
what_it_shows: Keys are generated and stored in HSMs; G1 uses a separate HSM domain and signing domain; customer-managed keys are available for customer data; key policies and rotation are owned by the groups that use them. HCP databases and backups are encrypted at rest with HSM-held keys

title: Group: backup vault configuration and backup job reports
source_system: Immutable backup vault at external provider X
what_it_shows: The vault at external provider X has immutability (vault lock) and a separate backup identity. Daily immutable copies of HCP control plane databases and nightly copies of SYS-P2 bill pay and ACH databases completed in Q1 2026

title: Group: central log archive policy and retention configuration
what_it_shows: The archive is in a separate account with write-once retention; only the log pipeline writes and a small security group reads. Retention is 1 year searchable and 7 years archived for all divisions

title: Group: external TLS configuration scan
what_it_shows: Console, API, portal and remote access endpoints accept TLS 1.2 or higher with approved cipher suites

title: Group: training records (LMS completion, phishing results, content outlines, role-based training, acknowledgments)
what_it_shows: Annual awareness training shows 97% completion, with quarterly phishing exercises. Content covers social engineering, including adversary-in-the-middle pages and MFA fatigue prompts. HCP engineers complete role-based secure operations training before production roles; Payment Processing adds a payments fraud module and role-based training for its security team. Incident responders and division liaisons complete annual incident training. Rules of behavior are acknowledged at hire and each year

title: Group: personnel screening records, sanctions log and contractor agreements
what_it_shows: Background checks are recorded for all hires; G1 staff pass an enhanced check and are U.S. persons. HR applies and records sanctions for policy violations. Staff performance objectives include security. Contractors with HCP access sign security terms; Managed IT partner operators are not under the HCP personnel terms

title: Group: vendor master, third-party risk records and contract templates
what_it_shows: Two follow-the-sun support vendors, located in countries that are not countries of concern under 28 CFR Part 202, can see support tickets and logs; their screening records show sanctions list checks and no check of ownership or control by covered persons. Acquisition contract templates carry security requirements. The supply chain risk management plan covers hardware, firmware and software suppliers; critical suppliers are assessed each year by SOC 2 reports, questionnaires and on-site reviews for hardware vendors

title: Group: vendor assurance and agreements for shared-service suppliers
what_it_shows: On file: SOC 2 Type 2 reports for the identity SaaS vendor, the SIEM and SOAR vendor, the EDR vendor and the RMM vendor; the provider agreement and SOC 2 report of external provider X; the third-party model service terms (no training, no retention). The RMM vendor contract has no incident notice clock and no model change notice for its agent feature

title: Group: AI use inventory and tool discovery
source_system: Procurement records; SaaS discovery; SYS-G1 app list; division model registers
what_it_shows: Ten AI uses were found: the SOC alert triage and automated response service (since 2025-11), the Cloud Hosting customer support assistant, fleet failure prediction and abuse and fraud detection, the Managed IT runbook automation agent (unattended since 2026-03) and consulting delivery assistant, Payment Processing transaction fraud scoring (since 2024) and merchant underwriting, an engineer coding assistant, and an enterprise generative AI assistant pilot

title: Group: Group AI Standard and Group AI council charter, adopted 2026-04-20
what_it_shows: The standard requires registration before use, tiering with the repository rubric, council approval of High-tier uses, written owner consent for AI actions in regulated environments, data scope limits for model context, and re-assessment on material change. The council is chaired by the Group Chief Risk Officer. The SOC triage service, the runbook agent and the fraud model were in use before the adoption date

title: Group: enterprise risk profile and division risk registers, Q1 2026
what_it_shows: The enterprise risk profile and division registers use the NIST SP 800-30 method and are reviewed each quarter. The Payment Processing register lists division systems and, from 2026, the reliance on SL-1 and the Managed IT RMM, without a separate assessment of those paths

title: Group: internal audit charter and 2026 audit plan
what_it_shows: Group internal audit reports to the board audit committee and neither designs nor operates the controls it assesses. The 2026 plan schedules the common control assessment with division samples from 2026-07-06 to 2026-08-28

title: Group: intercompany agreement register
what_it_shows: No intercompany agreement binds the Cloud Hosting or Managed IT division to Payment Processing safeguards terms (16 CFR 314.4(f)) or a PCI DSS responsibility split. The HCP federation trust with the Managed IT legacy tenant has no written interconnection terms, and the alert context sent to the model service is not described in an information exchange record

title: Group: legal determinations and counsel memos
what_it_shows: Group legal decided in 2023 to treat Payment Processing as a financial institution under 16 CFR 314.2(h) and to apply Part 314 to all consumer and cardholder information it handles. Counsel confirmed in 2025 that hosting for bank customers is a covered service under the bank service provider rule. The group is a CCPA business; whether the cybersecurity audit rules reach it is under counsel review. Counsel is reviewing whether Colorado SB26-189 reaches merchant underwriting

title: Group: corporate SaaS inventory, incident retainers and cyber insurance policy
what_it_shows: SYS-G4 holds the productivity suite, HR information system, ERP and finance, and IT service management. A forensic firm (through the insurer's panel) and outside breach counsel are on retainer; the group cyber insurance policy is in force for 2026

title: Cloud Hosting: customer agreements and customer records
source_system: Contract management system; customer relationship management
what_it_shows: About 38,000 business customers and about 290,000 customer console identities on SL-1, including about 260 banking organizations and about 900 health care customers under BAAs; about 4,100 SL-1 tenants are operated by Managed IT engineers through the partner-operator role with each tenant's contractual consent. The customer agreement requires incident notice within 72 hours of confirmation; the SLA is 99.99% multi-zone and 99.9% console and API. Maintenance notices go to bank customers 10 days ahead. CEO and CIO contacts for banks are held by account teams in the CRM, not in one register

title: Cloud Hosting: bank customer designated contact register
what_it_shows: Bank-designated contacts are on file for 182 of about 260 bank customers (70%)

title: Cloud Hosting: BAA register and templates
what_it_shows: BAAs cover about 900 health care customers of the HIPAA-eligible SL-1 services; the standard BAA requires breach notice within 10 calendar days; notice terms are not collected in a register. Subcontractor BAAs are signed with the support tooling vendor and the backup vault provider

title: Cloud Hosting: G1 FedRAMP certification records and package
source_system: FedRAMP secure repository; Government Cloud compliance records
what_it_shows: G1 holds a legacy FedRAMP Moderate agency authorization (2023-03-15, civilian agency sponsor), now recorded as a Rev5 Class C certification on the Agency path; no 20x certification. The package is documents and spreadsheets in the legacy secure repository, with no JSON outputs, and its index is current to 2026-03. The parameter table uses the legacy FedRAMP-defined values. The boundary list covers G1 infrastructure and the HCP-G partition; SYS-G1, SYS-G2 and the AI triage service are not listed. Data flow diagrams cover internal G1 flows, not the G1 log flow to the group SIEM and on to the model service. The third-party list names the identity SaaS and SIEM vendors as leveraged services and does not list the model service

title: Cloud Hosting: 2026 FedRAMP annual assessment report and 2027 engagement letter
what_it_shows: The annual independent assessment by a FedRAMP Recognized assessment service was completed on 2026-03-20; the 2027 assessment is booked to start 2027-02-08. The 2026 scope was selected under the legacy annual selection worksheet and did not include some listed controls (for example SC-45(1) and SI-4(23)); implementation evidence was mostly screenshots and exports

title: Cloud Hosting: G1 monthly continuous monitoring deliverables and POA&M
what_it_shows: Monthly legacy deliverables (POA&M, scan files) go to agencies; monthly calls are held with the sponsoring agency only. Long-running items are carried on the POA&M with deviation requests. Remediation targets are CVSS-based; critical and high findings are triaged within 2 days and others within 14 days. Major changes are notified to the sponsoring agency only, through legacy significant change requests

title: Cloud Hosting: G1 agency, DIB customer and federal contract records
source_system: Contract management system; G1 runbook library
what_it_shows: 27 federal agency customers and about 140 DIB customers that store CUI; agencies order G1 under federal contracts that include FAR 52.204-21, 52.204-23, 52.204-25 and 52.204-30. Agency-specific incident reporting procedures are on file for 21 of 27 agencies. The DFARS addendum for DIB customers commits to access and damage assessment support and does not describe the malware submission step. Two Cloud Hosting staff hold DoD medium assurance certificates for DIBNet; DIBNet steps and host imaging steps are not in the G1 runbook; G1 logs are kept 1 year

title: Cloud Hosting: FedRAMP communication, configuration guide and tenant default records
source_system: FedRAMP Marketplace; Government Cloud compliance records
what_it_shows: A FedRAMP Security Inbox (role mailbox) has been listed on the Marketplace since 2026-01; Emergency messages page the Cloud Hosting division CISO and the Government Cloud compliance director. The Secure Configuration Guide for top-level administrative accounts was published in 2026-02 for SL-1 and G1. Tenant defaults require MFA for tenant root owners at creation, PIV-based federation for G1 root accounts, and validated cryptographic endpoints for G1 tenants

title: Cloud Hosting: G1 cryptographic module inventory
what_it_shows: FIPS 140 validated modules are recorded for the documented G1 services, including the key service the SYS-M2 enclave uses. Module and update stream validation status is not recorded for two services: the managed database proxy and the object storage gateway

title: Cloud Hosting: G1 incident procedure and federal incident response coordinator rota
what_it_shows: The G1 incident procedure follows the legacy FedRAMP incident communications model; it has no PAIN rating step, and reports are written by hand as emails. The federal incident response coordinator rota has one person overnight

title: Cloud Hosting: HCP architecture and design documents
what_it_shows: Documents describe both HCP partitions (commercial: R1, R3, R4; G1: G1-A and G1-B), the policy engine that authorizes every request against tenant IAM policies with isolation enforced again in the data plane, workload identity and mutual TLS between services, the separate G1 policy engine, identity domain and keys, deny-by-default flows between partitions with only security logs leaving G1, snapshots and images shareable only by the owning tenant, management networks separate from customer networks with BMCs reachable only from bastions, memory and storage scrubbing and cryptographic erase, API schema validation, the design standard, the criticality analysis (policy engine, signing keys, run-command service), and the interconnection register

title: Cloud Hosting: HCP role, partner-operator and support access configuration export
what_it_shows: About 6,400 Cloud Hosting workforce members hold HCP roles. The partner-operator role is held by about 1,900 Managed IT engineers and allows run-command on every tenant assigned to the Managed IT division (about 4,100), not scoped to an engineer's client team; access is standing and federated from the Managed IT legacy tenant, with 12-hour sessions and tokens not bound to a device. Support engineers act only through case-linked, customer-approved access that ends when the case closes. The HCP access runbook sets operator, break-glass and support access procedures. Customer console sessions end after 12 hours or 1 hour idle; customer IAM locks accounts after 10 failed sign-ins in 15 minutes

title: Cloud Hosting: HCP logging configuration, event catalog and inventory export
what_it_shows: The HCP logs every console and API request, run-command execution, support access, partner-operator action, policy change and key operation, plus BMC and hypervisor manager events; records carry identity, federation source, target tenant and resource, action, source address, request ID, result and time. A release cannot deploy if its logging library tests fail. The HCP inventory is generated from the deployment system and the hardware asset database, and inventory and operating metrics feed monthly reviews; customer data access is through approved, logged paths

title: Cloud Hosting: HCP change, pipeline and signing records
what_it_shows: HCP changes go through the pipeline with peer review, automated tests (static and dynamic analysis, API parser fuzzing, tenant isolation tests) and staged rollout; emergency changes are reviewed within 1 business day; only the pipeline can deploy, with break-glass under two-person approval. Baselines are code with protected branches, signed commits and reproducible builds. Change records have no FedRAMP significant change field. Releases, images and guest-agent packages are signed with HSM-held keys and verified at deploy, with integrity checks every 24 hours. The dependency report blocks unsupported components. HCP service credentials are short-lived workload identities; the few static secrets are in the secrets store with 90-day rotation. Threat models are updated for new features

title: Cloud Hosting: HCP and fleet scan, patch and firmware reports
owner: Cloud Hosting data center operations director
what_it_shows: Weekly authenticated scans of HCP hosts and continuous image scans; network devices and BMCs scanned monthly, with fix validation not recorded for them. HCP services are patched through the pipeline; hypervisor and BMC firmware follow a quarterly cycle with emergency updates for exploited vulnerabilities. Configuration drift is detected and reverted on HCP clusters

title: Cloud Hosting: 2026 penetration test report and bug bounty summary
source_system: Testing firm report; bug bounty platform
what_it_shows: An external firm tested the console, API and partition boundaries in Q1 2026; a public bug bounty runs continuously

title: Cloud Hosting: HCP contingency plan, failover and restore test records
what_it_shows: The HCP contingency plan covers zone and region loss for both partitions, with reconstitution runbooks that rebuild services from code and check integrity before reopening the API. The HCP runs active in at least two regions per partition. Failover tests run twice a year (last 2025-11) and covered single-zone and single-region loss only. Quarterly restore tests of HCP databases are recorded. Capacity is planned per region with headroom targets

title: Cloud Hosting: data center physical security and media destruction records
owner: Cloud Hosting data center operations director
what_it_shows: 17 company-operated data centers (15 commercial in R1 to R5; G1-A and G1-B) and 41 edge points of presence. Entry uses badge plus biometric, mantraps, cameras and guards; G1 and CDE racks are in cages; access lists are role-based and reviewed each quarter, with G1 access limited to U.S. persons. Failed and retired drives are shredded on site with certificates of destruction. Facilities have multi-zone power, cooling and network, and generators with 72-hour fuel

title: Cloud Hosting: edge services, DDoS and status page records
what_it_shows: The console, API and customer endpoints sit behind SYS-H4 DDoS protection and rate limiting; group zones are also served by a secondary DNS provider. The public status page is hosted outside SL-1 and G1 and shows current status, with no 30-day history or machine-readable feed

title: Cloud Hosting: SL-1 SOC 2 Type 2 report (period ending 2025-06-30) and ISO/IEC 27001 certificate
what_it_shows: The SOC 2 Type 2 report covers Security, Availability and Confidentiality for SL-1 Commercial Cloud for the 12 months ending 2025-06-30. Its system description does not mention the partner-operator path. Customers are expected to manage their own users and MFA, choose replication, and approve partner-operator and support access. The Cloud Hosting division holds ISO/IEC 27001 certification

title: Cloud Hosting: customer IAM settings and MFA coverage report
what_it_shows: MFA is available to all customer users and required for tenant root owners since 2025; about 61% of other customer administrator users have it enabled. Customer account owners are verified at sign-up by payment instrument and business verification; terminated customers' data is deleted within 30 days with cryptographic erase

title: Cloud Hosting: supply chain receiving, inventory and award procedures
owner: Cloud Hosting data center operations director
what_it_shows: Hardware comes from approved vendors with secure shipping and firmware attestation and authenticity checks on receipt. The receiving procedure checks the approved vendor list, the software inventory is checked, and federal orders are checked at award; none of the three has a step for FAR 52.204-23, 52.204-25 or 52.204-30 reporting. The hardware bill of materials review is manual

title: Managed IT: client contract and service records
source_system: Professional services automation and ticketing (SYS-M1); contract management
what_it_shows: About 2,900 client organizations and about 380,000 client servers and endpoints under the RMM. About 190 banks and about 120 credit unions; about 210 health care clients under BAAs with breach notice terms from 10 to 60 days and no notice register; about 150 DIB clients (CUI enclaves managed for 18); 11 federal civilian agency contracts with FAR 52.204-21 (6 subcontracts, all with the flowdown); 9 DoD subcontracts with DFARS 252.204-7012. No ESP responsibility matrix or evidence package for DIB clients' assessments is in the contracts. A subcontractor BAA is signed with the RMM vendor

title: Managed IT: bank client designated contact register
what_it_shows: Bank-designated contacts are on file for 121 of about 190 bank clients (64%); fallback contacts are kept by account teams

title: Managed IT: legacy identity tenant configuration

owner: Managed IT division security and compliance lead

Leaver processing runs the next business day. Migration to SYS-G1 is planned for 2027-03-31

title: Managed IT: RMM tenant configuration, user and role export, and agent inventory
what_it_shows: One RMM tenant serves all about 2,900 clients and internal uses. Named technician accounts federate from the legacy tenant; roles are assigned per client team and are not in a quarterly certification. A script can be sent to many clients with one approver. Agents are installed on about 380,000 client systems, on 140 Payment Processing settlement-support servers in the CDE connected-to segment, and on the management servers of the SYS-M2 enclave. RMM audit logs are kept 90 days by the vendor default and are not forwarded to the SIEM. The script library is in version control

title: Managed IT: division security supplement v2024
owner: Managed IT division security and compliance lead
what_it_shows: The supplement was last aligned in 2024-05. It allows push MFA for technicians, 12-hour sessions, single-approver scripts and 90-day RMM log retention

title: Managed IT: CUI enclave SSP, network design, SPRS record and 2024 self-assessment
source_system: Federal programs records; G1 tenant console

The enclave SSP and asset inventory list enclave assets, without the RMM tenant or its agents. The NIST SP 800-171 basic self-assessment posted to SPRS on 2024-02-12 shows 96 of 110 requirements fully met. No C3PAO is engaged

title: Managed IT: enclave incident procedure, DIBNet certificate records, subcontract files and prime correspondence
owner: Managed IT federal contracts compliance officer
what_it_shows: The enclave incident procedure includes a snapshot and evidence hold step and a malware submission step; it has no step for giving the DoD report number to the prime (252.204-7012(m)(2)(ii)) and has not been tested. One person, the federal contracts compliance officer, holds a DoD medium assurance certificate. Two lower-tier subcontracts under the DoD work include the 7012 clause. Primes have told the division that CMMC Level 2 (C3PAO) would be required at the next option periods in 2027

title: Managed IT: consulting workspace permissions review
what_it_shows: Federal contract information from the 11 civilian agency contracts is stored in the general consulting workspace, where all consultants can read project areas; there is no separate area for FCI

title: Managed IT: client privileged access broker configuration and logs

title: Managed IT: service operations records

what_it_shows: PSA and RMM data used to manage client services; patching and vulnerability scanning reports for managed servers; change approval records for RMM jobs; recovery support records; capacity of the service desk and RMM licensing; wipe certificates for returned devices and offboarding records for client data at contract end; the continuity plan for an RMM outage, whose workaround (clients' own remote access) has no recorded test at scale

title: Managed IT: AI runbook automation agent configuration
what_it_shows: The RMM vendor's agent feature, using a hosted model, reads client tickets and has run 12 approved runbooks (service restarts, disk cleanup, patch retries) without a human since 2026-03

title: Payment Processing: program volumes, sponsor bank agreements and license register
source_system: Platform reporting; contract management; licensing records
what_it_shows: About 210,000 merchants, about 2,300 billers, about 14 million enrolled consumer bill payers and about 3.1 billion card transactions a year.
